sowhat.text: Financing stays open but is getting pricier: high yield spreads widened 12 bp to 326 bp and a Fed hike is priced for 9 Dec. A tech and AI selloff hurts stock-funded deals, while power and grid assets stay in demand, as GE Vernova's Trench deal shows.

pitch: Stocks sold off Friday. The S&P 500 fell 1.8% to about 7,580, its worst day since June, and the Nasdaq fell 2.9% as investors worried that AI companies are spending too much cash. Intel dropped nearly 29%. The 10-year yield eased to about 4.94%, but futures still show roughly a 70% chance of a Fed hike on December 9. Oil rose about 2% to 104 dollars on the Iran war, and Exxon and Chevron beat on profit. On deals, GE Vernova agreed to buy Trench Group for about 9 billion dollars, and DoorDash is buying Instacart for around 17 billion. Credit spreads widened a little but are still tight enough for deals.

quiz.q: Where did the S&P 500 close on Friday 30 Oct, and how much did it fall?
quiz.a: 7,580, down 1.8%, its worst day since June.

quiz.q: Why did the Nasdaq fall 2.9% on Friday?
quiz.a: Worries that AI spending is too high and burning cash: Intel fell 28.6% on a weak forecast, Nvidia fell 4.2%, and Amazon's free cash flow was negative $42.4B.

quiz.q: Who advised Triton on the sale of Trench Group to GE Vernova?
quiz.a: Bank of America and Morgan Stanley advised Triton; Goldman Sachs and UBS advised GE Vernova.
options: Bank of America and Morgan Stanley

chat.a: The S&P 500 fell 1.8% to 7,580, its worst day since June, and the Nasdaq fell 2.9% on worries that AI spending is burning too much cash. The 10-year eased to 4.94%. For bankers, the question is whether the tech wobble slows stock-funded deals.
chat.tip: Lead with the S&P, then the AI reason.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: WTI rose 2.1% to $104.12 on the Iran war, and Exxon and Chevron beat on profit. Oil above $100 keeps energy cash flow strong, which supports capex and energy M&A. Peace talks would pull it down and escalation would push it up.
chat.tip: Name the Iran swing factor in both directions.

chat.a: GE Vernova agreed to buy Trench Group from Triton for $9B, about 13x 2028 adjusted EBITDA, a grid equipment deal. Goldman Sachs and UBS advised the buyer; Bank of America and Morgan Stanley advised Triton. DoorDash is also buying Instacart for about $17B.
chat.tip: Name the advisers; bankers will ask.

chat.q: What are you watching this week?
chat.a: The October jobs report on Friday 6 Nov, about +55K expected, because it feeds the odds of a Fed hike on 9 Dec, near 70% now. Also Apple and Palantir on Monday as a read on AI demand after the tech selloff.
chat.tip: Tie each event to the Fed or AI theme.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year is 4.94% now. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Long-duration companies with most value in the terminal value fall the most.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then who is hit hardest.

chat.q: How would a tech selloff change M&A activity?
chat.a: The Nasdaq fell 2.9% and Intel fell 28.6%, so stock currency is worth less and tech targets reprice. High yield spreads widened 12 bp to 326 bp, still tight, so cash deals stay financeable. Buyers shift toward cash and hard assets like grid equipment.
chat.tip: Separate stock-funded deals from cash deals.

chat.q: How do the Fed and the 10-year affect M&A financing right now?
chat.a: The Fed held at 3.75–4.00%, but futures price about a 70% chance of a hike on 9 Dec. The 10-year is near 4.94%, so debt is costly, yet spreads of 326 bp for high yield and 89 bp for investment grade show buyers can still borrow. DoorDash lined up a JPMorgan bridge loan for Instacart.
chat.tip: Separate the base rate from the credit spread.
